definitions.explanation: An exceptional, almost supernatural level of talent or the person possessing it. The character {鬼|おに} (demon, spirit) suggests talent so extreme it seems inhuman. Often used to praise artists, directors, musicians, and other creative figures.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{映画|えいが}{界|かい}の{鬼才|きさい}だ。
examples.english: He is a genius of the film world.

examples.japanese: {鬼才|きさい}と{呼|よ}ばれる{画家|がか}の{作品展|さくひんてん}。
examples.english: An exhibition by a painter called a genius.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}くして{鬼才|きさい}の{名|な}をほしいままにした{音楽家|おんがくか}が、{新作|しんさく}を{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: The musician who earned a reputation as a genius at a young age has released a new work.

notes:
Literally "demon talent" — the {鬼|おに} (demon/spirit) implies talent so extraordinary it borders on the supernatural.

USAGE:
{鬼才|きさい} is a strongly laudatory term, used mainly in media, criticism, and literary writing. It appears most often as an epithet preceding a person's name or title: {鬼才|きさい}・{黒澤明|くろさわあきら} (the genius Akira Kurosawa). It is more dramatic and literary than {天才|てんさい}, carrying a nuance of dark brilliance or unconventional originality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鬼才|きさい}と{呼|よ}ばれる: to be called a genius
- {鬼才|きさい}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}: possessor of extraordinary talent
- {鬼才|きさい}{監督|かんとく}: genius director
- {鬼才|きさい}ぶりを{発揮|はっき}する: to display one's genius

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {天才|てんさい}: genius — the most common word for genius; neutral and broadly applicable, without the dramatic "demonic" nuance
- {秀才|しゅうさい}: brilliant person — implies academic excellence and diligence more than raw creative power
- {異才|いさい}: exceptional talent — similar to {鬼才|きさい} but less dramatic; emphasizes being different rather than supernaturally gifted
